label: Ghost kitchens
h1: An AI phone host for ghost kitchens
seoTitle: AI phone answering for ghost kitchens | ROAL
description: An AI phone host for ghost kitchens that answers calls, takes pickup orders, shares hours and menu details, and sends clean kitchen tickets.
lead: Ghost kitchens get busy fast. A missed call can be a lost pickup order, a delayed answer, or a caller who gives up and hangs up.
question: How can an AI phone host help a ghost kitchen take more pickup orders without adding more phone work?
answer: ROAL answers the ghost kitchen phone, takes pickup orders from your live menu, and sends a clean ticket to the kitchen screen. It can also answer hours, address, parking, and menu questions, then hand off allergy-sensitive or manager requests to staff with a summary. You can forward calls only when busy or unanswered, or send all calls to the host.

pains.title: Pickup calls come in during rushes
pains.body: Lunch and dinner rushes can stack up fast. If your cook is bagging orders and the phone rings again, someone has to stop what they are doing.

pains.title: Menu questions slow the line
pains.body: Callers ask the same things over and over. They want to know if a bowl comes with rice, whether a spicy sauce is mild, or what time pickup ends.

pains.title: Missed calls become missed orders
pains.body: Ghost kitchens often live on phone orders and repeat customers. If a caller gets voicemail, they may call the next place on their list.

howItHelps.title: Takes pickup orders from the live menu
howItHelps.body: ROAL can take items, sizes, modifiers, and notes from the menu you already have. If someone wants a chicken shawarma wrap with extra garlic sauce and no onions, it can capture that clearly.

howItHelps.title: Handles the common questions
howItHelps.body: It can answer hours, address, parking, and menu questions on the spot. That keeps simple calls off your counter staff during a rush.

howItHelps.title: Sends a clean kitchen ticket
howItHelps.body: Each completed order becomes a ticket on the kitchen screen with the caller name, phone number, ready time, and items. That helps your team start cooking without retyping anything.

howItHelps.title: Lets you forward calls only when you need it
howItHelps.body: You can forward all calls, or just when the phone is busy or unanswered. That makes it easier to fit into a small kitchen with a tight team.

sections.h2: What a ghost kitchen phone host should handle
sections.body:
A ghost kitchen phone host needs to do a few simple jobs well. It should answer fast, take pickup orders, and keep the order details clean. That means sizes, modifiers, sauces, no-onion notes, and the caller’s phone number all need to come through clearly.

It also helps when the host can answer the basics without interrupting the kitchen. For example: "What time do you close?" "Where do I pick up?" "Do you have veggie options?" "Is the spicy chicken very hot?" Those are the calls that can slow your team down one by one.

If you want to see the setup flow, start with [How it works](/how-it-works).

sections.h2: A simple setup for a small kitchen
sections.body:
You do not need a long project to get started. At /try, paste your restaurant website, Google Maps link, or just your name and city. ROAL reads your public menu, hours, and address, then builds a phone host in about two minutes.

You can test-call it in the browser before you go live. Then claim the host, forward your existing number, and choose whether it handles all calls or only busy and unanswered calls. If your menu changes often, you can upload a menu in any format and keep the host current.

If you want a quick overview before setting it up, see [ROAL for ghost kitchens](/for/ghost-kitchens).

sections.h2: A worked example for rush hour
sections.body:
Say your kitchen gets 12 missed calls on a Friday dinner rush. Some callers want pickup for two chicken bowls, some ask if the biryani is still available, and one person needs an order with a nut allergy note. That is a lot to juggle when the line is deep.

With ROAL, the phone host can take the routine orders, quote a ready time, and pass the allergy-sensitive call to staff with a summary. Your team still stays in control, but the phone does not keep pulling someone away from the grill or prep table.

If you want to compare options, look at [AI phone host vs voicemail](/compare/voicemail).

faq.q: Can ROAL take pickup orders for a ghost kitchen?
faq.a: Yes. ROAL is built to answer calls and take pickup orders from your live menu. It collects items, modifiers, notes, the caller’s name, and phone number, then sends a clean ticket to the kitchen screen.

faq.q: Can it handle menu and hours questions?
faq.a: Yes. It can answer common questions like hours, address, parking, and menu items. If it runs into something it cannot answer, it sends it to your inbox so you can teach it once.

faq.q: Does it take card numbers over the phone?
faq.a: No. ROAL does not take card numbers over the phone. Payment happens at pickup or however your restaurant already takes payment.

faq.q: How do I get it on my existing phone number?
faq.a: You keep your current number. ROAL gives each location its own phone line, and you forward your existing number to it. You can forward all calls or only busy and unanswered calls, then turn forwarding off any time.

faq.q: What does it cost for ghost kitchens?
faq.a: ROAL charges $0.90 per completed phone order, meaning a confirmed order whose ticket reached the kitchen screen. There is no monthly fee, no setup fee, no per-minute fee, and no contract. Calls, questions, and test calls are unlimited and free.
